newsitem.title: SPAIN: New case of swine fever in Spain not yet confirmed.
newsitem.headline: New case of swine fever in Spain not yet confirmed.

text.p: Spain's northeastern province of Lerida has yet to confirm the possibility of a third separate outbreak of swine fever, an official told Reuters on Tuesday.

"The results of the analysis are still pending. We're planning a press release either today or tomorrow. At present we can't add anything," the spokesman in Barcelona's agriculture department said when asked about press reports of a fresh outbreak.
A farmers' association added that after two outbreaks were detected in Lerida, effective measures such as slaughter and a transport ban had been adopted to control the problem.

"These cases of swine fever, all of them in pigs imported from the Netherlands, were completely isolated. Despite this, the sickness spreads very fast, so we took the right measures to stop it short," an official for a regional farmers association in Lerida told Reuters.

Since the disease had appeared around 14,000 pigs had been slaughtered, but he added "each day they are more, because they are killing all the animals in the area, not only the ones which are proven to be infected".

He said economic damage would be limited because farmers would get full compensation at market prices for sick pigs which were slaughtered, paid 70 percent by the European Union, 15 percent by the Spanish state and 15 percent by Catalonia's regional government.
Other pigs killed, but proved not to be infected, are sold to animal food producer firms, he explained.
Farmers said there is a total of about two million pigs in the province.
Counties affected by the transport ban are Pla D'Urgell, Urgell, Noguera, Segria and Garrigues.
